name: Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH
summary: Blankstahl Werdenfels is a family-owned bright-steel bar maker founded in 1961, with 200 staff and 98.2 M EUR turnover. It is financially sound (equity 39.3 %, credit index 148, unchanged) and we are a small account to it (0.4 % of its turnover). It is reviewing small accounts and focusing on customers with volume, and it now proposes a new price basis with an AS-14404 surcharge clause for the 1.4404 bar, with a recent quote 3.8 % above the current price.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 % price change. Above 2 %, the internal pricing committee decides (meets every two weeks). The owner is personally involved and has offered an open-book walk-through.

negotiation_pattern: Opens modestly (mean ask -0.01 %) and has settled on average 2.86 pts below its ask, every time at or below the opening figure. In the last round it asked +2.5 % and settled +0.7 % on part:370011, asked +3.0 % and settled -0.3 % on part:370012, and asked -0.6 % and settled -4.2 % on part:370010. It does not fight on price but expects substance. The owner twice offered to explain hourly rates and material costs to settle prices, so a fact-based, open-book discussion works better than pressure. Its sales director has signalled three times that small accounts are under review.
wants: volume and account relevance (more parts, higher quotas)
a fair, transparent price basis, ideally a material-specific surcharge clause (AS-14404) for 1.4404
respectful, fact-based treatment and recognition of its open-book offer
reliable on-time payment (we pay late 90 % of the time)
protects: unit_price on part:370010: wants the new AS-14404 basis and quoted 6.06 vs 5.84 current
anything above a 2 % price move without pricing committee approval
its focus on volume customers: unlikely to spend effort on a small, demanding account

trades.give: volume_per_year up: award new part:370020 (quote:7200016) and/or raise part:370010 quota above 20 %
trades.get: unit_price on part:370010 held at 5.84 or within the 2 % sales authority instead of 6.06
trades.why: It explicitly prioritises customers with volume, and we are only 0.4 % of its turnover.

trades.give: accept the AS-14404 surcharge clause for part:370010 (index_clause)
trades.get: symmetric clause (decreases passed on), material share no higher than 0.8, deadband kept, base fixed at today's level, no extra premium in the base price
trades.why: This is its current request. Granting the structure lets us control the terms.

trades.give: contract_months: 24–36 month extension of the framework agreement
trades.get: price within 2 % on all parts plus a binding OTD improvement plan towards the 95 % target
trades.why: A family firm values long-term commitment, and the contract runs out on 2026-12-31.

trades.give: accept the owner's open-book walk-through (hourly rates, material)
trades.get: split of material vs conversion cost to justify the base price and the index material share
trades.why: The owner offered this twice. Taking it up shows respect and gives us facts.

trades.give: commitment to pay on time at 30 days net (no change to payment_days)
trades.get: goodwill on price and on security of supply for single-source part:370011
trades.why: We pay late 90 % of the time. Fixing this costs us nothing and removes an irritant.

arguments.point: We can bring additional volume (part:370020) if the overall price package is right. This makes us a volume customer rather than a small account.

The existing contract already has an index clause (PPI-C2431, 80 % material share, 3 % deadband). Prices have already moved with it (part:370012 is now 143.39 vs 131.74 quoted in 2025). A new clause must not double-count material increases in the base price.
OTD has been 81–84 % for four quarters against the 95 % target in the quality agreement. Any price increase should be linked to delivery improvement.
Its history shows settlements well below the opening ask. A 3.8 % ask on part:370010 has room to come down.

avoid: hard pressure or threats to shift volume: we are a small account, and it may simply deprioritise us
pushing on part:370011, which is 100 % single source with no alternative
ignoring or brushing off the owner's open-book offer
demands that need more than a 2 % move without allowing for the two-week committee cycle
accepting an asymmetric AS-14404 clause or a base price that already includes surcharges
tone: Respectful, personal and fact-based. Acknowledge the long relationship and the owner's openness, frame it as a long-term partnership with more volume, and avoid ultimatums.
red_flags: Small-account review: risk of deprioritisation, worse service or walk-away, mentioned three times
part:370011 is single source (100 %, 0 alternatives): high supply risk
OTD 81.0 % and drifting down vs the 95 % contractual target
Deadline about 2026-11-01: 60-day notice for price changes and to stop the automatic 12-month extension of the contract ending 2026-12-31
AS-14404 alloy surcharge could import nickel and molybdenum volatility on part:370010
We pay late 90 % of the time, which erodes goodwill

evidence.claim: Family-owned since 1961, 200 staff, 98.2 M EUR turnover, equity 39.3 %, credit index 148 (stable)
Reviewing small accounts and focusing on volume customers; we are 0.4 % of its turnover
Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval, which meets every two weeks
Owner offered an open-book walk-through of hourly rates and material, twice
Proposes a new price basis with an AS-14404 adjustment clause for part:370010
New quote for part:370010 at 6.06 vs current 5.84 (+3.8 %); new part:370020 quoted at 96.37/100
Framework agreement ends 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice; existing PPI-C2431 index clause with 0.8 material share and 3 % deadband
Scorecard green with low ppm (32), but OTD 81.0 % vs 95 % target; flat fee EUR 150 per complaint

indicators.credit_index: 148 (12 months ago 148; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 82.7, ppm 58) → 2026Q1 green (otd 83.8, ppm 26) → 2026Q2 green (otd 82.5, ppm 38) → 2026Q3 green (otd 81.0, ppm 32)
